correctness.rationale: The greedy feasibility test is exact: prefix and suffix embeddings are in disjoint intervals around a fixed covered position. Composing embeddings proves transitivity, and any shorter cover of a factor extends by the surrounding letters. Thus the primitive-candidate filter is sound and a missing primitive length precludes longer primitive words. Independently, I enumerated every nonempty position subset for each host represented by first-occurrence alphabet normalization. Grouping subsets by their spelled word and OR-ing their position masks directly tests all covers, with no primitive bound or greedy predicate. Weighting one-symbol representatives by 3 and all others by 6 gives the full 3^n texts at each length. This returns zero through 10 and one normalized failure at 11, with the exact two covers of length 6, hence the six labeled failures.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration verifies the finite classification only, not arbitrary-length structure.
